problem: Estimate $\sqrt{{e}^{0.2}+0.1}$ using a differential $\text{d}f$ of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{e}^{x}+y}$ at the point $(0,0).$
worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2\sqrt{{e}^{x}+y}}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{e}^{x}+y}}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(0,0),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =\frac{{e}^{0}}{2\sqrt{{e}^{0}+0}}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{e}^{0}+0}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(0+Δx,0+Δy),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈\frac{1}{2}\,Δx+\frac{1}{2}\,Δy
$$

Note that 

$$
\sqrt{{e}^{0.2}+0.1}=f(0.2,0.1),
$$

so we want to move to the point $(0.2,0.1).$

Moving from $(0,0)$ to $(0.2,0.1),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =0.2-0=0.2, \\ Δy & =0.1-0=0.1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈\frac{1}{2}(0.2)+\frac{1}{2}(0.1) \\  & =0.1+0.05 \\  & =0.15.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that the value of $f$ increases by about $0.15.$ Consequently, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.2,0.1) & ≈f(0,0)+0.15 \\ \sqrt{{e}^{0.2}+0.1} & ≈\sqrt{{e}^{0}+0}+0.15 \\  & =1+0.15 \\  & =1.15.\end{aligned}
$$
